feedback.worked_solution:
First, we rearrange the equation and isolate $\operatorname{sec}⁡x$:

$$
\begin{aligned}2\operatorname{sec}⁡x-3\sqrt{2} & =\sqrt{2} \\ 2\operatorname{sec}⁡x & =\sqrt{2}+3\sqrt{2} \\ 2\operatorname{sec}⁡x & =4\sqrt{2} \\ \operatorname{sec}⁡x & =2\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Recall that $\operatorname{sec}⁡x=\frac{1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}.$ Therefore the given equation is equivalent to

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡x=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{2}}.
$$

Then, we find the principal value of $x,$ rounded to three decimal places:

$$
{x}_{1}=\operatorname{arccos}⁡(\frac{1}{2\sqrt{2}})≈1.209
$$

Our first solution lies in the $1$st quadrant and has a reference angle of ${\theta }_{R}≈1.209.$ Since $\operatorname{cos}⁡x>0,$ the second solution must lie in the $4$th quadrant, and it also has a reference angle ${\theta }_{R}≈1.209.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13989949/assets/2c58ae6d53b409e4fac7c4fb5c4d96b08585b1c2ee8a4f1048f4461026d748af.png)

Since the second solution ${x}_{2}$ lies in the $4$th quadrant, we can find it using the reference angle as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & =2\pi -{\theta }_{R} \\  & ≈2\pi -1.209 \\  & ≈5.074\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, in ascending order and rounded to one decimal place, the solutions are $x=1.2$ and $x=5.1.$
